walkthroughs.body_html:
After Muhammad's ﷺ death in 632 CE, Muslims divided over leadership.

Sunnis followed elected caliphs (Abu Bakr first).

Shi'as believed Ali, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, was the rightful leader, and that leadership stays in the Prophet's family through the Imams.

Both share Tawhid, Qur'an and the Five Pillars.

Al-Qadr teaches Allah knows and decrees everything. But Muslims also have free will and are accountable.

The Qur'an: 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves' (13:11).

Shi'a teaching tends to emphasise human responsibility (Adalat — Allah's justice) more strongly.

Muslims revere Isa (Jesus) as a great prophet, born of the virgin Mary (Maryam — surah 19).

Muslims affirm Jesus performed miracles and will return at the end of time.

However, Muslims do not believe Jesus is God or the Son of God (this would be shirk). Most Muslims also hold that Jesus was not crucified but raised to Allah (Qur'an 4:157-158).
